Concurrently, VCP mutations disrupt the ubiquitin-proteasome system, crucial for protein homeostasis and cellular function, contributing to neurodegeneration seen in FTD/ALS. partners.mechanism_chain: CFTR pathogenic variant (rs750334497) —DISRUPTS→ CFTR (HGNC:2408); CFTR (HGNC:2408) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial ion transport and mucus clearance (GO:0007155); Epithelial ion transport and mucus clearance (GO:0007155) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens (HP:0000027); PSMD12 pathogenic variant (rs1479965114) —DISRUPTS→ PSMD12 (HGNC:23978); PSMD12 (HGNC:23978) —DISRUPTS→ Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome (HP:0030859); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Facial dysmorphism (HP:0001999); Proteasome-mediated protein degradation (GO:0006508) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Pathogenic variants in CFTR lead to dysfunction in epithelial ion transport and mucus clearance, causing congenital bilateral aplasia of vas deferens. Concurrently, PSMD12, a component of the 26S proteasome, is implicated in Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome; its loss-of-function variants disrupt proteasome-mediated protein degradation, leading to a spectrum of phenotypes including facial dysmorphism and intellectual disability. The hypothesis is that dysregulation of the shared proteasome-mediated protein degradation pathway by both CFTR and PSMD12 dysfunction contributes to the distinct disease phenotypes.
